title: A Confused, Frustrated, Fragmented, Childish Political Rant
content:
Our institutions do not produce the future
They produce consumers in a stagnant society blinded by the monstrous amalgamation of superficial luxury and barbarism
We have forgotten what is sacred
We have forgotten how to live with purpose and desire for a higher life
Our blood is tainted and barbaric
But still, embrace it
The blood of revolutionaries
Amidst terror and oppression
We held our ground against colonizers, exploiters, and despots
We are a living testament of courage and fidelity towards freedom and dignity, be our oppressors foreign or our own blood
So why can’t we realize that the weak can become strong?

The ability to vote gives us an illusion of choice and freedom. “This representative is good for x reasons and bad for y reasons. This other one is a compassionate person etc.” The choices are all shit, that is the problem for me. They all seem different but oppress us in similar fashion. The same politicians who support bigger politicians, local and international, who form symbiotic relationships to owners of big private capital and wealth. A system that juggles the people’s discontent and anger between representatives and political theatrics. This “juggling” as a means of controlling the people’s dissatisfaction and revolutionary energy, turning systemic problems into controlled and manageable chunks that can be easily patched up by officials and private owners. 

We have made politics a consumable product that defines identity. People love identities. Identities are sources of fulfillment and purpose - the most in demand products of our confused consumerist society. What ideology do they buy into? In politics we see collective representation and cults of personality. If the USA represents freedom, money and liberal democracy, as to Martin Luther King with racial equality, Napoleon with meritocracy, the french revolution with equality and human dignity, Athens with democracy, Rome with the power of Law, Caesar as the republic incarnate, Communism with the march of History, Lenin and Stalin with revolutionary change with an iron will along their atrocities - What does the Philippines represent? What do the personalities represent? Rizal with the transformation of an uncultured population into higher consciousness through social polemics, literacy, and education. Bonifacio with the overthrowing of an oppressive order through necessary violent means. The Catholic church as the medium/means of immediate and unreflective access to an alien culture built throughout millennia, to inspire the mass into a higher shape of consciousness - not through words but through religious feeling, ritual, and faith. The American system implanted into our constitution. Free trade and consumer society, the English language which opens up a portal to generations of reflection on humanist and technological progress, the Anglo-saxon enculturation of Filipinos, higher education. And the digital commons and the internet, imported by alien corporations. Is this the essence of the Philippines? What is a Filipino? 

Again what exactly do our current cult of personalities represent? The Dilawan, Kakampink, Die Hard Duterte Supporters, and Marcos loyalists? What do they represent? Are DDS populist fanatics who are tired of the sensitive elites and their big words, do they vow for the rights of discriminated Filipinos looked down upon by their own fellow Filipinos? Do the Dilawans and Kakampinks represent liberalism, progressive laws, do they represent political correctness like in the USA, or do they just support their representatives because they have better rhetorics and pseudo-ideology than the other parties? Are Marcos loyalist nostalgic perverts who care more about state bureaucracy, competent functioning government, even with dubious and oppressive means, is he even competent? What about oligarchy and nepotism? The very leaders we put in power steal from us. They openly show their abuses of power and make them spectacles for the Filipino people, interpellate them into participants in their political theatrics. This is what happens when a society is granted economic, technological, and bureaucratic advancement without advancement in culture and ideology - the shape of consciousness is left behind and what remains is a machine that functions for the sake of functioning - no purpose, no ideal, no vision. We crave for a greater good to believe in, this void is fundamental to society and its progress. But when this craving is left to be satisfied by power hungry and barbaric individuals, we regress and create a backwards culture and society. We remain illiterate and uneducated and we follow the spectacles. We become drunk with our own lives - the next trend, the correct political party, social status, better job, more money, better lifestyle, better relationships - we try to fill a hole that can never be full or satiated.

I am aware that communism regresses into totalitarian terror, but wasn’t it a driving force of human consciousness? Capitalism lifted millions of people out of poverty, made access to education, health, and necessary needs accessible to a big population. But it is also the driving force of indescribable human inequality and ecological crisis.

People waste a lot of energy (but their fidelity for change in itself is a great honor) in these campaigns and feuds between divided followers. Is this not the perfect distraction to any genuine political act or event? While we are fueled with euphoric rage and self-satisfied ideals, don’t we affirm the current system? The same system that is the root of our problems.

We participate in capitalo-representative politics, its subtle systemic terror, and public theatrics and explicit violence while we leave true politics behind. Those who are hopeful of political social/liberal reform through the state and an elected representative will remain hoping. People who think that opinion and lofty humanitarian goals alone can change society (me for example) are being naive.

Non-party(decentralized) mass violence against the state is necessary. A constant flux that can break the inertia of societal decay. A politics with no active violence, left only with unrealized universal principles, is like change without change or revolution without revolution. If there is a reason for my apathy it is because I am neither capable of great violence nor do I affirm the status quo. I am suspended from any action. I choose to wait and carry the hatred. I still remain faithful to a fraternal, egalitarian, and liberal society. I hate elections, I hate the invisible strings behind the farcical drama. I am hoping for a genuine event (we are already seeing symptoms), a confusing and unprecedented event in the perspective of the present, that will be clear retroactively and become a mark in history.

Getting emotionally caught up in elections drains the energy of the common people and distract them from initiating genuine political acts.

What we need are long lasting institutions that provide social welfare and inspire the people towards their higher selves. Institutions that can guide human desire towards a better understanding of themselves and the world they live in. Institutions that are forgiving but not condoning, that create opportunities but not spoon feeding the people. Institutions that maintain healthy inequality and strives for an egalitarian society. Bureaucracy that can stop private owners into positions of absolute power, public officials who keep in check corporations and foreign powers, not suck up to them and support their oppressive regime.

This is the fantasy I give myself into. Optimistic that such institutions are possible. Pessimistic that our very human nature is geared towards self destruction.

title: Bunch of Non Sense
content:
Being alone is horrible. Not the metaphorical melodramatic kind but in the sense of social seclusion which takes away potential and possibilities. On the other hand, over socializing is exhausting and cuts possibilities instead of maintaining them. 

I love being alone with my thoughts. It keeps me grounded. I am condemned to wear multiple masks, and I presume others do the same. We fool ourselves to the point where we begin to believe our own lies. 

But I can never be alone. Not only because I want to keep my living prospects and lifestyle and weird habits but more so because there will always be the imaginary observer of my own mind and actions, and this judge is the shadow that will never leave me. Who am I even talking to right now? Sino ka man, tangina mo hehe biro lang

I learned from analysis that we make our own point of view of an external gaze or observer, and we judge our thoughts, actions, and behavior through the lens of this gaze whether it is acceptible or not. This judge is born from our desire and insecurities. We perform for this self-made superficial judge - it tells you which words are right, what behavior will embarrass and haunt you in your dreams, which opinions will make people accept or reject you. This judge is never satisfied, it will shit on your efforts. Shit and piss over your blood and sweat. We are our own severe judge and we are most critical of ourselves. 

I think this connects to the idea that how you judge others is a reflection of your own self-made judge. How you criticize others reflects your own insecurities, because you project your own oppressive judge unto the other person. It can make you feel validated because you pass the criteria after all, not that other person. 

That’s why we make masks. We try to negotiate with our human limits to elicit scraps of approval for our broken psyche. This mask could show others that “I might be ugly but at least I have a personality. I might be poor and looked down upon by people but I am genuine and hard working. I may not be the brightest of minds but I have the ability to care deeply about others. My mother does not love me … and so on.” 

It takes a genuine friend to listen and help you process unresolved problems. People do not need sensible advice in times of distress. They just want a mirror to help them clarify what went wrong and what went good, turn the whole escapade into a reasonable course of events and eventually forget the discomforting experience ever existed. What is not let out will spill in ugly, obscene ways. So we need to stabilize the gaze itself.

title: The Beauty of a Cold, Empty Wall
content: Why do I even do this. I prefer to enjoy things in private because I feel that there’s some sort of debasement to anything shared outside oneself. Flee from the market place, for so long have your spirit been hollowed, continuously stung and sucked by tiny pests and crushed by great men; in mud have you sunk and suffocated, flee to your heights, where clean air and endless ebb of honey overflows – something like that. The feeling Zarathustra gives to the solitary spirit is just profound and refreshing. Or maybe it’s just a way to preserve the ideal ego. It is undeniable that I feel, how do I put this, a psychosomatic refreshment whenever I go back to his ideas, as if inhaling air in the mountains for the first time. But even Zarathustra had his going under. Even he felt alone in the night, his proud light feigned someone or something to shine for. One might argue that he is simply overflowing, that his gifts do not care for any reciprocation, a mere indifferent effect of his free spirit. I would argue that Zarathustra wanted an empty space to project his being. An indifferent gaze that acts and judges indifferently on behalf of people. In spit of his efforts to keep it all to himself, to retain his pure honey, overcome, and breathe freely with clean air; the endless rumination kept to himself, the ideas, experiences, the various overcoming over tragedies – a life as lived art, his affirmation of life in a world disavowed from any fundamental meaning or grand narrative or overseeing and graceful God – I think we wanted to write for himself. He wanted to create a perfect barrier by constructing a beautiful soul. In the end, he wanted a silent horse he could talk to – no “yea” or “nay,” just a pure medium, an empty canvas he can pour his heart out. What his deepest longings, what he has not told nor written to anyone besides himself – we can never know. However I argue that what he proclaim to be gifts to others, I think to be gifts for himself. He never wanted devout guardians of his ideas. He never wanted recognition by the people, inttelectual chairs and all the dogma and popular opinions. His gifts for himself I say, becaues he wanted to make himself clear to himself. To grasp his own being. What better way to make it clear than talking to an empty wall?

title: What once was, I remember as the present
content:
In a strange land
	Lonely and dreary
		Comes a hopeful warmth
			For a heart so weary

title: A Fine Tuesday
content:
I look at the mirror and see a deformed slab of meat. I can’t help but imagine what lies
underneath. Skull and bones, molding, decomposing, dissipating into dust; an image of 
peace, eternal peace and quiet. But no, I see someone, breathing and sentient. Surely he’s  alive, maybe.
 Who is he? What does he want? How is this fuckwit capable of living?
Only the devil knows. 

At times I envy the dead. How can they be so … empty. Living is too un empty. One day
 you’re full of purpose and delight, the next day you see your dreams crushed before your
 eyes. You continue living in a merry go round of love, longing and despair.

Life is neither empty nor full. While death, eternal, empty and complete. How can the dead
leave us to fend for ourselves? What, in the name of justice, right do they have to be
so quiet? They built this world and left it behind to confusion. They passed the curse of
life with their lust and greed for an eternity of generations. How can they be so selfish?
In death they have already gained everything they could ever want, yet they still
insist to be “more.” 

Dying is too easy compared to living. It only takes a few moments to vanish into
 nothingness. Living is too insolent to admit its decay. It foolishly persists that there is more
 besides its march to emptiness.  I envy the dead, I admit. I hate them for the same reason.

title: Order and Chaos
content:
Winds of past renown
	Treads on ice over abyss
		Beyond, calls a precious world of ours

A quiet desperation for life shared with warmth
	Invites a wicked smile poised and cowled
		“Alas, you are ours”

Deep in the cold embrace of the singy-song flowing water
	In slips a shadow to the void drowned with whispering sorrow
		Bleeding eyes sift past, piercing into light growing prouder by the hour
			“We are one” its maddened grin howls

title: Writing for no reason
content:
Writing has always been therapeutic for me. When the world seems so loud and fuzzy, there is some peace I can take refuge to. 
I write not for the sake of other reasons. I write for the sake of writing itself. The most destructive and externally aimless activities
 are often the most profound.
